title: RAW excess moisture keeps its material role across animal-specific discharge branches
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. In Albertus' third-digestion account, excess moisture is separated through urinary filters in urine-bearing animals, while in others it remains mixed with faeces. A class condition changes the stated fate without deleting the material or turning alternatives into consecutive stages.

design.source_specific_content: The digestive sequence reaches the veins and their extremities. Excess water is separated through urinary filters in some animals that have urine; in others without it the water remains mixed with faeces.

design.question: Can one explicit stage-scoped material description feed two class-conditioned fate assertions, preserving what is being described when the excretory route differs?

proposed_content_schema.DECLARE_MATERIAL: DECLARE_MATERIAL(owner, digestive_episode, excessive_moisture_description) fixes the owner and local stage scope of the described material. Shared material-kind wording alone does not identify different physical portions or amounts.
proposed_content_schema.BRANCH: BRANCH(explicit_animal_class_condition, positive_body, other_class_body) scopes alternative descriptions to their stated classes. It neither asserts both branches for one episode nor orders them as successive stages.
proposed_content_schema.positive_body: Within the source's urine-bearing class, SEPARATE_FROM(moisture, locally described nutritive material, urinary_filter_route) expresses the stated separation with explicit participants and route.
proposed_content_schema.other_class_body: Within the contrasted non-urine class, REMAINS_MIXED(moisture, faecal_material) retains the moisture participant in a mixture description. It does not imply permanent bodily storage, nonexistence or an actually completed excretion event.
proposed_content_schema.composition: DECLARE_MATERIAL establishes the local participant description; BRANCH keeps that semantic role while class scope selects SEPARATE_FROM or REMAINS_MIXED. Any common target referent across clauses must still be expressed, not inferred from adjacency.
proposed_content_schema.scope_limits: No named species, absence of kidneys, quantitative conservation, exact chemical identity, anatomical modernisation or universal law for all animals is added. The word urine is the source classification; it is not silently replaced with a hidden organ predicate.
proposed_content_schema.stage_limit: The branch is embedded in the third-digestion account. It does not make two successive digestive stages, skip the fourth/member account or equate a named stage with an anatomical site. The plant paragraph remains separate full-unit content.

connected_cases.input: A written local digestive material description under the stated urine-bearing animal condition
connected_cases.consequence: The same locally scoped moisture role participates in a separation assertion with a urinary-filter route. No inference that all moisture or all material is expelled follows.

connected_cases.input: The corresponding local material role under the source's other, non-urine animal condition
connected_cases.consequence: The moisture is still represented, now remaining mixed with faeces. Absence of urine therefore cannot erase the moisture participant from this source account.

rivals.name: Sequential two-route itinerary
rivals.contract: Every animal first has urinary separation, then the same moisture is mixed with faeces.
rivals.consequence: It converts class-scoped alternatives into a temporal chain. A fixed written conditional must not allow that unexpressed sequence.

rivals.name: No urine means no excess moisture
rivals.contract: The negative urinary condition deletes the moisture participant or treats its quantity as zero.
rivals.consequence: It conflicts with the source's statement that the material remains mixed with faeces. Changing route and mixture status does not warrant deleting the participant.

rivals.name: Separate class-specific clauses
rivals.contract: Use independently named animal classes and independent material/fate statements without a shared branch constructor.
rivals.consequence: This can retain the same physiology and is a serious equivalent vocabulary. A shared written material description and controlled scope would be needed to favor the proposed construction.

costs.unbound: All target class conditions, material participants, mixture ownership, stage scope, route values, clause boundaries and ordered constructions. Analytical schema counts are not word counts.

The narrowly proposed reuse is the source's linked no-urine/still-present-in-mixture contrast with alternatives scoped inside one stage; root must compare exact primaries before selecting.
design.minimum_next_step: Review branching and material-reference predecessors. If the negative-urine/positive-mixture dependency is not already represented, author one complete admitted unit containing both written class scopes and their material/fate assertions. Preserve all source clauses and alternate reader forms; do not infer body or material identity from a shared noun.
design.decision_changing_result: An explicit shared material description with class-scoped alternative fate assertions could distinguish this branch reading from a sequential itinerary or absent-material model. If all scope and identity come from commentary or independently guessed nouns, retain RAW without a compositional claim. This task supplies no observed target consequence.
